sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Aries begins the zodiac year and brings self-direction, initiative, courage, and the next beginning into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: What do you desire so fiercely that it can’t be ignored?
sun_corpus.opening: Aries is the spark that sets the wheel of the zodiac into motion. The Sun enters this sign at the start of the zodiac year, bringing your attention back to what you want to initiate and where you are ready to lead yourself. This is a season to act on the desire that keeps returning, especially when you already know the first move.
sun_corpus.tension: Aries moves quickly, which means desire can arrive before the plan is complete. Not every impulse deserves action. Impatience, anger, or the need to prove something can push you toward a reaction that solves the feeling of being stuck without solving the situation itself.
sun_corpus.development: Aries learns through trial and error. Taking the first step gives you information that planning cannot produce on its own. It also clarifies boundaries: what you want, what you will tolerate, and what belongs to you to decide. This season favors choices that put your own direction back in your hands.
sun_corpus.close: Begin with the part that is clear enough. Learn from what happens next and adjust from there.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Aries is the spark that sets the wheel of the zodiac into motion.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: A decision can stay theoretical for weeks when what you actually need is one move that gives you something concrete to respond to.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Begin with the part that is clear enough, then learn from what happens next.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Taurus brings values, resources, self-worth, and what you are willing to cultivate into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: What do you truly value, and what would it take to support it in daily life?
sun_corpus.opening: The Sun enters Taurus, and your values become harder to separate from the way you spend your resources. What gets your time, money, attention, and care is what you are actively building, regardless of what you say matters to you. This month is a chance to put more behind the people, skills, work, and parts of your life you actually want to grow.
sun_corpus.tension: Taurus can turn preservation into a reflex. You can keep paying for something because you already invested in it, keep a routine because it is familiar, or keep supporting a relationship because the alternative feels uncertain. The longer something has been part of your life, the easier it is to confuse history with value.
sun_corpus.development: Look at the resources you actually have and how you are using them. A budget, calendar, recurring obligation, or skill you keep developing can tell you more about your priorities than an intention ever will. Taurus is interested in what can be cultivated, strengthened, and enjoyed over time, so invest in what still deserves your care.
sun_corpus.close: Put more behind what you want to grow. Let the rest stop taking resources simply because it always has.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Your values become harder to separate from the way you spend your resources.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: Time, money, attention, and care keep showing you what you are actively building.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Put more behind what you actually want to grow.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Gemini brings movement, conversation, learning, perspective, and the choices we make through language into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: Pay attention to the questions that change what you think, and the ones you use to avoid deciding.
sun_corpus.opening: Gemini Season begins on {{entryDate}}, inviting a shift toward movement, conversation, learning, and conscious curiosity. This is a time to notice what you’re saying, what you avoid, and why. Words are choices that reveal alignment or avoidance.
sun_corpus.tension: Without grounding, curiosity becomes avoidance. Words become noise. Another article, opinion, conversation, or possibility can help you understand something better, or it can give you one more reason to keep every option open. Notice when information is changing your understanding and when it is keeping you from choosing.
sun_corpus.development: Why do you believe what you believe? Who taught you that? And is it still true? Gemini gives you room to revisit assumptions, hear another perspective, and change your mind without treating revision like failure. Information becoming wisdom is the point: something you can actually use.
sun_corpus.close: Say what you mean and mean what you say. Let curiosity lead somewhere.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Gemini Season shifts attention toward movement, conversation, learning, and conscious curiosity.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: Another source or opinion can clarify the picture, or become one more reason to keep every option open.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Notice which question changes what you think, then let the answer lead somewhere.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Cancer brings home, family, emotional safety, care, memory, and the foundation underneath everything else into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: Your foundation affects everything you build on top of it.
sun_corpus.opening: As the Sun enters Cancer, we’re invited to shift from doing to feeling. The energy encourages you to come home to yourself. This season brings your body, home, family, and closest relationships into focus because the conditions around you affect how much of yourself you have available for everything else.
sun_corpus.tension: Care can become automatic with the people you love. You remember, adjust, protect, make room, and keep going because someone has to. Over time, support can quietly become one-directional, or a family role can survive long after the circumstances that created it.
sun_corpus.development: Tell yourself the truth about what feels supportive and what does not. What helps you feel safe enough to rest, speak honestly, take a risk, or ask for help? Which old family patterns are still shaping present choices? You can start with where you are now and strengthen the parts of your life that actually help you recover, connect, and keep going.
sun_corpus.close: The strongest growth begins at the roots. Give your own foundation the same care you keep offering everyone else.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Cancer Season brings your foundation back into view.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: Your body, home, and closest relationships affect how much of you is available for everything else.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Strengthen the parts of your life that actually support you.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Leo brings creativity, love, joy, self-expression, pride, recognition, and the courage to be seen into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: What makes your heart feel alive, and are you giving it enough room to exist?
sun_corpus.opening: As we transition from Cancer to Leo season, a new self begins to take shape, one rooted in safety and revealed through joy. What has been healing privately now wants expression. Leo brings the focus to creativity, love, pleasure, desire, and the parts of you that want to be seen without having to become someone else first.
sun_corpus.tension: Recognition matters, especially when you care about what you made or how you showed up. The trouble starts when a quiet response, a creative block, or someone else getting the attention makes you question the thing itself. Leo can chase the reaction so hard that the joy disappears from the work.
sun_corpus.development: Who sees you, loves you, and accepts you as you are? When you feel safe enough to stop bracing for ridicule or rejection, creativity has more room to open. Give time to the work, relationships, pleasure, and play that make you feel more like yourself. Your desire to be recognized is information too: it can show you what matters enough that you want your name attached to it.
sun_corpus.close: Let yourself be seen for something you actually care about. Give your joy enough room to become part of your life.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Leo Season brings creativity, love, joy, and visibility into focus.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: A quiet response can make you question something you care about faster than the work itself deserves.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Give your attention to what makes your heart feel alive, even before anyone else reacts.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Virgo brings daily systems, work, health, service, skill, and the details that keep life functioning into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: If the system keeps creating more work, the system needs attention.
sun_corpus.opening: Virgo Season is a reality check. Look at the systems you rely on every day and notice which ones actually support you, and which have become daily punishment disguised as productivity. Useful routines should make the day more workable. If they leave you feeling behind before the day even starts, something needs to change.
sun_corpus.tension: Virgo can spend so much time correcting the details that the correction becomes another job. You can track every habit, refine every plan, and still be exhausted because the structure itself is asking too much. Invisible work also accumulates here: the thousand small decisions that keep everyone else moving and only get noticed when they stop.
sun_corpus.development: Look for the repeat problem. Which task creates three more tasks? Which responsibility follows you home because nobody clarified who owns it? Where are you giving more time, care, or expertise than the arrangement gives back? Virgo is good at improvement. The best fix may be the one that removes unnecessary work instead of training you to carry more of it.
sun_corpus.close: Fix the part that keeps creating more work. Then let the rest be good enough to function.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Virgo Season is a reality check.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: A disciplined routine can still leave you exhausted if the structure itself is asking too much.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Fix the part that keeps creating more work.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Libra brings relationships, agreements, fairness, reciprocity, and the balance between self and other into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: Look at who keeps adjusting, who gets accommodated, and who has been doing the work of keeping the peace.
sun_corpus.opening: The Sun enters Libra at the September equinox, when day and night briefly meet at equal length. Then the balance shifts. Balance is a moment, not a state. Relationships work the same way; they need adjustment as needs, circumstances, and people change.
sun_corpus.tension: Libra wants harmony, which can make it tempting to treat conflict as evidence that something is wrong. Sometimes the most loving thing you can do is disagree. The scales become more useful when you stop judging the relationship by how peaceful it looks and start looking at who makes the decisions, who gives in, and whose needs keep becoming negotiable.
sun_corpus.development: This is where honest compromise and self-abandonment separate. Those scales reveal who's been putting their thumb on them. If one person keeps swallowing the disagreement, changing the plan, or doing more of the work so everyone else can stay comfortable, the arrangement is already telling you where the imbalance lives.
sun_corpus.close: Practice showing up as yourself in your relationships. This season teaches you the difference between keeping the peace and creating it.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Balance is a moment, not a state.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: A relationship can look peaceful while the same person keeps adjusting, giving in, or doing more of the work.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Look at what each person is actually carrying.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Scorpio brings transformation, intimacy, power, shared resources, endings, and what has been hidden or avoided into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: Name what has already ended so your energy can stop keeping it alive.
sun_corpus.opening: The Sun enters Scorpio, and what has been kept alive by habit, fear, or unfinished logistics becomes harder to ignore. Scorpio doesn't kill what's alive. It names what's already dead and asks why you're still propping it up. This season makes it easier to see what has expired even when the structure around it is still standing.
sun_corpus.tension: A relationship can end emotionally months before it ends logistically. A career can stop feeding you while the paycheck keeps you showing up. An identity can survive because everyone, including you, already knows the role. Scorpio brings the cost of preservation into view when the thing being preserved is no longer alive.
sun_corpus.development: Scorpio also speaks to shared resources, money, time, support, intimacy, and how power moves between people. Who owes what? Who carries the emotional intensity? Who gets to stay on the surface because someone else is doing the deeper work? Transformation becomes practical when the terms change, the truth is named, or the energy tied up in the old arrangement is finally released.
sun_corpus.close: Transformation isn't the breakdown, refusing it will be. Let what has ended make room for something that can actually live.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: What has already ended becomes harder to keep propping up.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: A relationship, job, or identity can keep running long after the part that made it meaningful has already ended.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Name what has ended so your energy can stop keeping it alive.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Sagittarius brings truth, belief, meaning, perspective, direction, and the story you are living by into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: What do you still claim to believe, and does your life reflect that belief?
sun_corpus.opening: Sagittarius is the sign of storytellers and philosophers, and this season turns your attention to the stories that have come to define your life. Some of those stories still give you direction. Others may have become too small, too old, or too disconnected from the person living them now.
sun_corpus.tension: Sagittarius can make a bigger story feel more important than the facts that complicate it. Optimism can keep you moving, but it can also keep you loyal to a plan, relationship, or worldview long after the evidence has changed. The question is what the story helps you see and what it helps you avoid.
sun_corpus.development: Gemini asks what you know. Sagittarius asks what it means in the bigger picture. Travel, study, teaching, philosophy, religion, publishing, and unfamiliar perspectives can all widen the frame, but expansion has to change something more than the view. Beliefs shape choices. Choices create direction. If the life you are building no longer reflects what you say you believe, the story needs another look.
sun_corpus.close: Reclaim authorship. Choose a direction that can hold the truth you know now.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Sagittarius Season brings the story you are living by into focus.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: A belief can guide you for years and still stop matching the life you are actually living.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Reclaim authorship and choose a direction that fits what you know now.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Capricorn brings time, responsibility, ambition, authority, accountability, and the structure behind long-term goals into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: What does the goal require from you, and is the structure strong enough to support it?
sun_corpus.opening: Capricorn Season brings accountability and pragmatism back into the room. A goal changes once you can see the time, responsibility, money, limits, and consequences attached to it. This is where ambition stops being an idea and becomes a structure you have to live inside.
sun_corpus.tension: Capricorn can keep climbing because stopping to reassess feels like losing ground. Responsibility also collects around the person who has proved they will carry it. If every plan works because the same person absorbs the pressure, that is part of the plan too.
sun_corpus.development: Saturn rules Capricorn, so time matters here. Doubt can be useful when it points to the weak part of the structure, the missing resource, or the responsibility nobody has accounted for. Think long-range: one year, five years, ten years. What would need to change, end, or be redistributed for the goal to remain worth pursuing?
sun_corpus.close: Build a structure that can support the life around the goal. Ambition gets more expensive when responsibility keeps landing on the same person.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: Capricorn Season brings accountability, time, and responsibility into focus.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: A plan can look successful while the same person keeps absorbing the pressure required to make it work.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Build a structure that can support the life around the goal.

sun_corpus.tldr_what: The Sun in Aquarius brings community, systems, individuality, innovation, and the future we are building together into focus.
sun_corpus.tldr_takeaway: Who do you stand with, what do you stand for, and what are your choices helping build?
sun_corpus.opening: The Sun in Aquarius illuminates the space between what has been and what could be. This is the season to get clear about who you stand with and what you stand for. The future becomes less abstract when your values start changing how you participate in the present.
sun_corpus.tension: Aquarius can see the flaw in a system long before there is agreement about what should replace it. Distance protects independent thought, but it can also become a way to stay above the mess while other people are still living inside it. Seeing what needs to change is the beginning of the work.
sun_corpus.development: Aquarius is traditionally ruled by Saturn, which gives the sign its relationship to systems, rules, responsibility, and the collective. Its modern association with Uranus adds disruption, experimentation, and the impulse to break from inherited structures. The useful question is what your difference contributes. Can the idea become a tool, a community, a policy, a network, or another way of organizing resources and people?
sun_corpus.close: Bring something back to the collective. Build the future in a form other people can actually use.
sun_corpus.fallback_hook: The Sun in Aquarius illuminates the space between what has been and what could be.
sun_corpus.fallback_lived: Seeing what is wrong with a system matters more when the insight changes something for the people living inside it.
sun_corpus.fallback_turn: Turn the idea into something other people can actually use.

Its modern association with Uranus adds disruption, experimentation, and the impulse to break from inherited structures. The useful question is what your difference contributes. Can the idea become a tool, a community, a policy, a network, or another way of organizing resources and people?

Bring something back to the collective. Build the future in a form other people can actually use.

retrograde_modifiers.copy: Mars retrograde reminds us that even the most blazing fires need time to rest and rekindle. Mars retrograde invites us to slow down, and sometimes, our bodies enforce this lesson for us. When Mars, the planet of energy, drive, and vitality, moves backward, we’re asked to pause, reflect, and redirect. This can show up physically as illness, injury, or exhaustion, a clear signal that something needs our attention.

seasonal_context.copy: The March equinox marks the beginning of spring in the Northern Hemisphere and arrives at the same moment the Sun enters Aries. Day and night briefly meet at equal length before the days continue growing longer. The zodiac year begins here too, with Aries carrying the first spark of the new cycle.

The March equinox marks the beginning of autumn in the Southern Hemisphere and arrives at the same moment the Sun enters Aries. Day and night briefly meet at equal length before the nights continue growing longer. The seasonal light is changing direction while the zodiac year begins a new cycle.

The Sun enters Aries at the March equinox, when day and night briefly meet at equal length across the globe. The March equinox is one of the four turning points of the solar year, and Aries begins the zodiac year.

The Summer Solstice marks the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, a turning point where light peaks, then slowly begins its descent. The Sun enters Cancer at the same moment, shifting the focus from doing to feeling.

The June Solstice marks the shortest day of the year in the Southern Hemisphere, a turning point where darkness peaks and the light slowly begins to return. The Sun enters Cancer at the same moment, shifting the focus from doing to feeling.
The Sun enters Cancer at the June solstice, one of the four turning points of the solar year. The balance of light changes direction across the globe as Cancer Season begins.
The September equinox begins autumn in the Northern Hemisphere. Day and night briefly meet at equal length, then the nights continue growing longer. Libra Season begins at the same turning point.
The September equinox begins spring in the Southern Hemisphere. Day and night briefly meet at equal length, then the days continue growing longer. Libra Season begins at the same turning point.
The Sun enters Libra at the September equinox, when day and night briefly meet at equal length before the balance shifts again. Libra Season begins at this turning point of the solar year.

The Winter Solstice marks the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. From here, the light slowly begins to return. The Sun enters Capricorn at the same moment, beginning a season concerned with time, responsibility, and what can be built to last.

The December Solstice marks the longest day of the year in the Southern Hemisphere. From here, the light slowly begins to recede. The Sun enters Capricorn at the same moment, beginning a season concerned with time, responsibility, and what can be built to last.
The Sun enters Capricorn at the December solstice, one of the four turning points of the solar year. The balance of light changes direction across the globe as Capricorn Season begins.
